spec: ACT1_KEEPER_JOIN v0.1.1 (design repo, private): the Wickerglen investigation, the orchard lean and the Keeper join
_about: Ours, not a design copy. After the crackdown's dawn release Ilse sends the holder to Vincent Chi (the debrief's last lines live in detail_zz_crackdown.json). Route 2 opens on story.warden_met (D1551) so the holder can reach Wickerglen; Imogen's battle and the lit lamps wait for the enrolment (r2_lead is hidden on a crackdown save until story.keeper_cadet). An old save (no crackdown) reads every gate as before. Save stays pixelpets.save.v2; every flag here is a new additive story.* key.

_placeholders.note: PLACEHOLDER copy (Story/June to replace; OPEN_DECISIONS rows D1545-D1560). Every line in this file is a placeholder, including the Constable's name. 'Eleven' Walklings is a PLACEHOLDER number; Vincent Chi's name check is pending (D1524); the jar line and his lean line (story.lean_keep) are the engineer's draft. D1562: the enrolment's lanyard line (no question) and the post-recall Lantern Council lines are the engineer's draft until §4.7 and §4.9 are rewritten.

Vincent Chi's body (chi_hut) and the first-step trigger (chi_hut_first, scene chi_meet) come with the weir hut room (WEIR_HUT, detail_zz_weir_hut.json); his lines are keyed here. 4.6-4.7 (D1510, D1511, D1553): the lean waits for Vincent Chi's report on a crackdown save; Tobin's battle stands for an Open lean; Ilse enrols at the Lodge; the lanyard face takes effect at Juniper (either body). D1561: a Glimmerwell-held Fernbrook keeps one Keeper post; the Constable at the plaza post (K1's fbplaza:post) says why.

looks._note: PLACEHOLDER (Sprites). Vincent Chi: an ex-Keeper Scout gone off the wire. A slate raincoat, no Keeper green, no Glimmerwell wine or mint; grey buzz cut, a satchel of papers. PAL keys only.

chi_meet: A low hut over the water. Papers pinned on every wall. Someone has been busy.
Ilse sent you. Good. No poles out here. The wire can't hear the water.
I walked Scout for the Keepers once. Now I just write down what nobody asks me to.
He drops a pressed leaf into a glass jar on the sill. One jar of six.
Wickerglen's lost eleven Walklings this month. Nobody's looking. So I am.
Both sides work that glen. Work a shift with each. Look at what they don't show you.
Imogen's crew needs hands by day. A Keeper Scout keeps watch at dusk. I'll be here.
chi_report: Well? Tell me what you saw. All of it.
chi_hub: Six Seals, held by permit. The ban didn't stop Fernbrook's Seals. It sent them somewhere.
Lamps that hum, and Walklings that listen. Fen saw it, and wrote it up. Then the tanks came.
A list with no heading is still a list. Show Ilse, not me. I don't want my name near it.
You watch more than you work. Good. Write it all down.
You keep your hands busy. Fine. Keep your eyes busy too.
I can't tell you who signs. I can tell you it's one story: the Seals, the lamps, the tanks.
Go home by the orchard. Fen's crates are still at the gate.
shift_day: New hands? Lovely. Lenses, sweetie. Three lamps. Quarterly review is Friday.
shift_lamp_w: You wipe the glass. The lamp hums under your hand, slow as a heartbeat.
shift_lamp_n: You wipe the glass. The lamp hums under your hand, slow as a heartbeat.
shift_lamp_e: You wipe the glass. The lamp hums under your hand, slow as a heartbeat.
shift_ledger: A ledger on the lid. LAMP STOCK. FERNBROOK ALLOTMENT: 6 SEALS. HELD BY PERMIT.
The permit number is there. The name under it is smudged past reading.
Six Seals. Fernbrook hasn't given out one since the tanks came.
That's the boring paperwork, sweetie. Partners only. Lenses!
Stock is stock. It keeps the lamps happy. Don't make me write you up.
shift_end: Good shift! Have a bright day. Come back once you've got a team worth showing me.
night_watch: Captain's orders: watch the glen, touch nothing. It's their ground, by permit.
Dusk. The lamps come up, one by one. The glen goes very quiet.
The lamps pulse, slow and even. In the roots, small heads lift.
A Fuzzwick walks out of the dark toward the nearest lamp. Then another. Then three.
{pet} leans toward the hum. You put a hand on it, and it stays with you.
Under the lamp, a crate stands open. They climb in on their own. Nobody has to push.
Third night this week. I write it down. It goes up the line. Nothing comes back.
Commander's papers came with my orders. Fernbrook. Holders with Seals.
A list of names, no heading. Yours is the newest line.
Above me. Above my Captain too, I think. I just carry it.
Morning. The crates are gone. The lamps hum on, as if nothing walked to them at all.
ilse_call2: Your Keeper1 buzzes in your pocket. WARDEN ILSE.
Things are changing. In the shadows. I can feel it from here.
Come home tonight. Before anyone else sends for you.
Keeper Amos hurries up from the Lantern House, out of breath.
{name}. Warden Ilse sent word down the wire. Things are changing, she says. Come home tonight.
enrol: Show me what you saw. ... Six Seals. And a list with your name at the bottom.
Your name is on an old list from the war. I'd rather you were on mine.
I pulled every string I have left. The rank and file still listen to a Warden.
As of tonight, you're a Keeper Cadet. You answer to me, and only to me.
You've already got their ear. That's worth something to me.
They'll want you more for saying no. They always do.
So. Wear the pin where everyone can see it. Or wear their lanyard, and tell me what they do.
Then walk tall. And remember your home.
Juniper's offer still stands. Take it. Smile. Remember your home.
So. You'll wear their lanyard, and you'll tell me what they do.
Juniper's offer still stands. Take it. Smile. Remember your home.
enrol_lanyard: You came back! I knew you had sparkle. Trial lanyard, as promised!
Yay! Welcome to the partnership, {name}! Brighter by nature.
Juniper presses a thin handset into your hand. No crest. It still sits on their wires.
rpt_1: Ilse's letter asks one thing: what did you see? Nothing else.
You think of Quinn's back room, and the quota.
And the soft click, and the way {pet} listens now.
You think of Hale's Seal, and the quarry vote that passed by three votes.
You write it all down, just as you saw it.
You fold the letter with half of it left out.
I'll write it down. The Court will want to see this.
rpt_2: Ilse's letter asks one thing: what did you see? Nothing else.
You think of the Signal Review, and the screen that answered.
You think of the Lantern Council, and the coast road.
You write it all down, just as you saw it.
You fold the letter with half of it left out.
Keep your eyes open on the coast. Remember your home.
ilse_recall_call: Your Keeper1 buzzes in your pocket. WARDEN ILSE.
Come home. You've worn their colours long enough.
A Lantern House runner finds you with a folded note. COME HOME. I.
recall: Take it off. Keep it in a drawer, not on your coat.
Tell me the last of it. Then you're mine in daylight.
You tell her all of it: the manifest, and Dorian's quay.
You tell her all of it: the Brinewick crate.
You tell her some of it. The rest you keep.
Captain Lumen has asked for you. The capital is waiting, Cadet.
cadet_sendoff: Tell me the last of it. Then you're mine in daylight.
You tell her all of it: the manifest, and Dorian's quay.
You tell her all of it: the Brinewick crate.
You tell her some of it. The rest you keep.
Captain Lumen has asked for you. The capital is waiting, Cadet.
hc_council: Both Seals are here. Fernbrook first, then Cobblecrest. The lanterns watched you walk.
Ilse's letter arrived ahead of you. She said the Seals would.
You walked the coast in their colours, and came home in ours. Ilse vouches for every step.
The chart on the wall shows the coast road, already lit. Lumen taps the capital instead.
The coastal road to Brinewick is on the board. We are opening it. Walk it carefully.
The chart names the road. A small light beside it flickers on.
THE ROAD AHEAD · Route 3 to Brinewick, from Cobblecrest's east road.
